Q2 FY27: (262.967) + 456.363 + 42.230 + 1.378 - 0.002 - 0.017 = 236.985 [6]. SBC is excluded from EBIT and recorded as its own quarterly line (sbc); FY26 SBC-related charges 36.5% of revenue. EPS = company non-GAAP diluted (SBC excluded); any multiple must read peers on the same basis.

drivers.label: Net revenue retention rate (company definition: trailing-2-year cohort of capacity customers, product revenue year 2 / year 1; reported at quarter end)
drivers.source: Ex.99.1 'Financial Highlights' / Key Business Metrics: Q1 FY26 124%, Q2 125%, Q3 125%, Q4 125% [1-4], Q1 FY27 126% [5], Q2 FY27 126% [6] (10-Q: 126% at 2026-07-31 vs 125% at 2026-01-31 [7]); history Q4 FY24 131% [11], FY25 128/127/127/126% [12-15]. Definition: cohort = capacity customers using the platform in the first month of the first year of the trailing 2 years; NRR = cohort product revenue year 2 / year 1; churned customers count as zero [6].
drivers.derivation: Identity (per Kilian's spec): product revenue(q) = product revenue(same quarter a year earlier) x nrr + new_cust. Q3 FY27 128%, Q4 129%: the reported rate is trailing-12-month and lags the quarters (quarterly product growth 33.9%/36.8% in Q1/Q2 FY27 vs TTM product growth 31.1%/32.6% and NRR 126% [5,6]; the Q3 guide is +37-38% y/y [6]), so the TTM rate rises as H2 FY27 rolls in (CFO: third consecutive quarter of acceleration, existing-customer consumption is the driver [6,7]). FY28 129/127.5/126/124.5%: the AI step-up (CoCo 9,100 accounts, +2,000 in Q2 [6]) laps. FY29 123->120%, FY30 119->117%: the fade the company showed as the base grew (131% Q4 FY24 -> 124% Q1 FY26 [11,1]) plus Iceberg tables (storage and some compute outside Snowflake, 10-Q risk factor [7]), Databricks warehousing ($1.5B, >100% growth [23]) and price-performance cuts passed through. Check: the TTM residual implied by our quarters is 6.0% of TTM product revenue at Q4 FY27, 5.2% Q4 FY28, 3.9% Q4 FY29, 3.1% Q4 FY30 (FY25-FY26 actual 2.8-3.2%, Q2 FY27 5.0%): the FY28 reported rate could run ~1-2 pt above this path at the same revenue. Variant: downside -4 pt, upside +3 pt on every forecast quarter (scenarios).
drivers.why: The consumption metric the company and the Street use for existing-customer growth; the debated item (AI consumption up, Iceberg/storage and price cuts down).

drivers.label: Product revenue not explained by NRR: customers outside the NRR cohort (new logos of the last ~24 months, on-demand) + acquisitions ($M a quarter; identity residual)
drivers.derivation: Q3 FY27 135, Q4 110: the H1 FY27 residual (78, 118) is not all new-customer revenue: it holds the TTM lag of NRR (quarterly existing-customer growth runs ahead of the TTM rate) and Observe; as the TTM NRR catches up (128-129%) the residual falls back. FY28 80/72/68/66, FY29 66-70, FY30 70-74 = 2.3-3.0% of product revenue, the FY25-FY26 structural level (quarterly residual 1.4-4.9%, mean 2.9%; TTM 2.8-3.2%), growing slowly with net customer adds (616-740 a quarter [4,7,8]). Variant: downside -25%, upside +20%.
drivers.why: Keeps the NRR identity closed: every dollar of product revenue is either existing-cohort (nrr) or this residual; makes new-logo and acquisition revenue visible.

drivers.label: Non-GAAP product gross margin (non-GAAP product gross profit / product revenue, Ex.99.1)
drivers.source: Ex.99.1 reconciliation 'Non-GAAP product gross profit': Q1 FY26 754.124 / 996.813 = 75.7%, Q2 833.631 / 1,090.496 = 76.4%, Q3 879.165 / 1,158.377 = 75.9%, Q4 921.462 / 1,226.631 = 75.1% (FY26 3,388.382 / 4,472.317 = 75.8%) [1-4]; Q1 FY27 1,002.695 / 1,334.329 = 75.1%, Q2 FY27 1,114.084 / 1,491.861 = 74.7% [5,6]. Guide: FY27 non-GAAP product gross margin 75% (2026-02-25 [4]) cut to 74.0% (2026-09-02 [6]). 10-Q: GAAP product GM 71% vs 72%, 'costs attributable to newly launched product capabilities ... not yet reached economies of scale', partly offset by better cloud-infrastructure discounts [7].
drivers.derivation: FY27 guide 74.0% on product guide 6,070 [6] implies H2 GP 4,491.8 - H1 2,116.8 = 2,375 on H2 product 3,243.8 = 73.2%; the company beat its FY26 guide (75% -> 75.8%), so Q3 74.0%, Q4 73.5% (FY27 74.3%). Variant: downside -2 pt (AI mix at lower margin, hyperscaler pricing), upside +1 pt.
drivers.why: Makes AI gross-margin dilution visible; op margin = gross profit - opex is computed, not a driver.

Extend the approved set's FY30 (revenue 12,398, non-GAAP OI 2,651 = 21.4%, SBC ~18-19.5% of revenue) three years at 18/16/14% growth -> FY33 revenue 19,346; non-GAAP op margin 28% (the set's ~2 pt a year opex leverage continued) = 5,417; SBC 13% of revenue (set path falls ~1 pt a year) = 2,515; interest income 250; owner earnings (5,417 - 2,515 + 250) x 0.75 = 2,364; x 35x (SBC-costed P/E for mature growing software, near DT's 38.2x and above TDC's 17.5x GAAP NTM P/E in peers.md) = 82.7B; / 419M shares (382M x 1.015^6.25) = $197 at Jan 2033; discounted 5.25 years at 10% = $120 at the horizon. Not driver-linked.

sbc_treatment.note: FY26 SBC 1,599.5M (F43; SBC-related charges incl. payroll tax 1,710.7M, 36.5% of revenue). The set's EBIT is non-GAAP (SBC excluded), so shares grow +1.5%/yr net of buybacks (sbc_treatment 'dilution'); the multiple legs read non-GAAP peers on the same basis, and the 0.20-weight custom leg costs SBC explicitly (13% of FY33 revenue). FCF TTM 1,195.3 (F95) less SBC TTM 1,641.9 (F46) = -446.6M: on an SBC-costed basis SNOW is not yet profitable.

reasoning: Lane base-rates. (1) Own history [29]: 63 overlapping 12-month windows since the 2020 IPO give P10 -43%, P25 -23%, median +2.4%, P75 +25%, P90 +44% (log sd 0.38) - a flat-median, very wide distribution, wider than the ±25-35% large-cap norm; realized vol 64% in the last year, 52% ex-earnings [30]. (2) Earnings events [30]: 14 prints, median |move| 14.1%, 8 up; guide record 10/10 product beats (median +4.6%) and first annual guides beat by a median +4.5% (FY24 a miss), so the beat habit is known and priced. (3) Multiple regime [27]: EV/sales 67x (FY22) -> 23.8x -> 22.3x -> 16.7x -> 13.9x (FY26), TTM 19.3x now: re-rating since the trough rests on the AI consumption acceleration; base rates for high-multiple software say multiples compress as growth fades, so I keep the default k=0.8 shrink toward the 7.8x peer median and do not add a premium. (4) Macro [28,34]: prediction markets on 2026 Fed cuts are dated poorly and disagree; no rate effect is put in the numbers. Model: the approved quarterly driver set is used exactly (my view: I accept the nrr path; on base rates the risk to Q3 product is upward given the 10/10 record, while the FY29-30 NRR fade to 117% is reasonable given NRR fell from 158% to 126% in four years). Value: EV/sales 12.1x (w 0.55) $311.80, non-GAAP P/E 98x (w 0.25) $369.56, SBC-costed maturity leg $120 (w 0.20) -> $287.88. METHOD FIT: GAAP losses mean GAAP P/E and EV/EBITDA do not apply; non-GAAP multiples ignore ~30% of revenue of SBC, so they are weakened and the non-multiple SBC-costed leg is added (not driver-linked). Cases: the set's driver deltas plus P/E -40 / +55 turns, sized to land near the own-history P10/P90 (engine 174.61 / 451.39). Research limited: 6 page fetches; Twelve Data statistics/estimates not in plan. Sources 1-23 are the approved set's filing/consensus sources (basic facts); of my 12 added sources 6 are in-lane (EV/sales history, prediction markets x2, own price-history base rates x2, post-earnings press), 3 unlikely to be found by other lanes (StockAlarm EV/sales history, Oddpool, own post-earnings base-rate calc).
